title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1967-03-18
lineage: MR > ? > CD  > EAC > Cool Edit 96 (Resampled to correct pitch) > SHN

ai_review.summary: A landmark early‑67 show with scorching “The Same Thing”, Viola Lee Blues and Cream Puff War; the audience tape is fair/uneven but listenable for its era.
ai_review.review: This recording captures one of the most exciting pre‑Summer‑of‑Love sets – the band rides high on Jerry Garcia’s ferocious Guild “Starfire” tone, delivering a blistering “The Same Thing”, soaring Viola Lee Blues and rare early performances of Cream Puff War and Golden Road.  The sound is an audience source with hiss, occasional drop‑outs and volume spikes that make it only fair by modern standards, yet the musical energy more than compensates for those flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive comments about the performance (many 4‑5 ★) and a consistent appreciation of the historic setlist outweigh the mixed remarks on audio fidelity, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss, mud‑dy mids and occasional drop‑outs; some volume spikes where Jerry’s guitar overpowers the mix.  Overall clarity is limited but captures the live atmosphere of a 1967 Winterland show.

poor_songs: Bobby Weir vocals on several numbers (warbly/out‑of‑tune)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Fast, frenetic first set that builds into an explosive second set featuring rare early tracks; the pacing feels natural and the rare songs are well‑placed for maximum impact.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s hollow‑body Guild/Starfire tone is described as scorching, ferocious and a highlight on virtually every song, especially “The Same Thing”, “Dancin'” and “Viola Lee”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass work is praised as brilliant and surprisingly sophisticated for 1967, providing the backbone of the band’s evolving chops.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s rhythm guitar is generally solid, but his vocals are repeatedly called warbly or out‑of‑tune on several tracks.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is occasionally buried by tape quality, yet his harmonica and bluesy vocals receive high praise, especially on “The Same Thing” and other blues numbers.
